documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Technology Usage Guidelines
documents.summary: An IT-owned guideline for all users: AI is welcomed with care, Copilot is recommended, and users must protect data, check output and follow academic-integrity policy. It also names OIT as enforcer and promises periodic review.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no course-level rule on whether students may use AI. It 'advocate[s] for fostering curiosity and responsible usage' and supplies IT security duties (data protection, review of output, risk assessment) while pointing academic questions to UAM 6,502 and 'disclose the use of AI in academic settings as appropriate'. With no stance of its own for coursework, it delegates.

units.why: The preamble says the university 'advocate[s] for fostering curiosity and responsible usage of AI tools', which welcomes AI use for everyone, so it is a permit/encourage default (P02), not a rule on a specific use.
units.anchor: we advocate for fostering curiosity and responsible usage of AI tools
units.frag_start: As AI tools continue to experience
units.frag_end: maintaining safety, security, and academic integrity across the institution.

units.why: The guidelines state they 'align seamlessly with existing University policies', tying AI use to current rules; P77 (comply with existing policy) fits better than P56 because it points to other policies.
units.anchor: designed to align seamlessly with existing University policies

units.why: The Purpose section sets the framework's aim and who it binds ('all students, employees, contractors, and third parties'), an institution-level preamble of purpose and scope (P56).
units.anchor: establish clean guidelines and requirements for the usage of AI tools

units.why: Says the university has no enterprise vendor contracts and 'Use of AI tools is at the discretion and risk of the user' with no guarantee of accuracy. No type covers a risk-transfer disclaimer, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Use of AI tools is at the discretion and risk of the user.
units.uncovered_note: The university gives no vendor contracts or guarantee for most AI tools and puts the use and its risk on the user.

units.why: Names Microsoft Copilot as the recommended tool for all users with a NetID, which is the institution-wide approved tool (P92), not a course tool (P17).
units.anchor: the University recommends Microsoft Copilot for AI-related tasks

units.why: 'imperative to adhere to all recommended data protection protocols' tells users to protect data and privacy when using third-party AI, which is P50.
units.anchor: imperative to adhere to all recommended data protection protocols

units.why: Warns AI output may be 'incomplete, erroneous, or influenced by biases' and that users must 'exercise diligence and critical judgement', matching verify-the-output (P31).
units.anchor: incumbent upon users to exercise diligence and critical judgement

units.why: States 'Human oversight and review are indispensable' for catching AI errors and bias; it is the same verification duty as P31, in a second sentence about human review.
units.anchor: Human oversight and review are indispensable

units.why: The Scope section says the guidelines apply to all users 'on computing resources owned or managed by the University', defining what the policy covers (P61).
units.anchor: applicable to all users engaging with AI tools on computing resources owned or managed

units.why: 'strongly advised not to share Sensitive, Confidential, or Regulated data on AI tools' is a data-protection rule with soft modality ('advised'), so should-not under P50.
units.anchor: strongly advised not to share Sensitive, Confidential, or Regulated data on AI tools

units.why: 'Users are required to meticulously review AI-generated content' to avoid misleading, biased or copyrighted material: a mandatory verification duty (P31).
units.anchor: Users are required to meticulously review AI-generated content

units.why: Before using an AI tool, users 'should initiate a vendor risk assessment' through OIT Compliance; this is institutional review of AI tools (P65).
units.anchor: users should initiate a vendor risk assessment through the Office of Information Technology

units.why: Says 'Adherence to academic standards policies (UAM 6,502) is crucial', linking AI use to existing integrity policy (P77).
units.anchor: Adherence to academic standards policies

units.why: Users are 'encouraged to familiarize themselves with relevant policies', a duty to learn the applicable rules (P78).
units.anchor: encouraged to familiarize themselves with relevant policies
units.fit_note: Refers to relevant policies in general, not specifically to each course's AI rules.

units.why: Users are encouraged to 'disclose the use of AI in academic settings as appropriate', a soft disclosure rule (P24), softened by 'as appropriate'.
units.anchor: disclose the use of AI in academic settings as appropriate

units.why: 'Be vigilant against potential phishing schemes' is security awareness about AI-era threats (P75).
units.anchor: Be vigilant against potential phishing schemes
units.frag_start: Exercise caution when utilizing AI tools
units.frag_end: Maintain a heightened awareness of security risks.

units.why: Advises choosing 'reputable and well-established AI tool providers' and avoiding risky third-party access; closest is prefer vetted tools (P50), though it does not name a vetted list.
units.anchor: opt for reputable and well-established AI tool providers
units.fit_note: Asks users to choose reputable providers rather than prefer university-vetted tools.

units.why: 'Users are responsible for adhering to these guidelines' and acting ethically sets a general duty to comply with the guidelines (P77).
units.anchor: Users are responsible for adhering to these guidelines

units.why: Department heads and supervisors must make teams 'aware of and compliant with' the guidelines; assigns an implementing role to units (P80).
units.anchor: ensuring that their respective teams are aware of and compliant
units.fit_note: Names department heads and supervisors as responsible for team compliance.

units.why: They 'should also facilitate access to training and educational resources', which is AI training for staff and students (P70).
units.anchor: facilitate access to training and educational resources as needed

units.why: 'OIT oversees the implementation and enforcement of these guidelines' names the office that owns and enforces the policy (P80).
units.anchor: OIT oversees the implementation and enforcement of these guidelines

units.why: Users with Confidential or Regulated data (FERPA, HIPAA, etc.) 'must take all necessary precautions' against unauthorized access; a data-protection duty (P50).
units.anchor: must take all necessary precautions to prevent unauthorized access

units.why: 'Employees must use extreme caution when opening e-mail attachments' from unknown senders and flags phishing; security awareness (P75).
units.anchor: Employees must use extreme caution when opening e-mail attachments
units.fit_note: Concerns email attachments generally, not AI-crafted phishing specifically.

units.why: The university 'reserves the right to access and review' information and monitor systems to check violations of the guidelines. This is monitoring of users, not a type on the list, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: reserves the right to access and review such information under certain conditions
units.frag_start: While the University desires to provide
units.uncovered_note: The university reserves the right to access, review and audit information and systems to investigate problems or violations of the guidelines.

units.why: As a public agency, records in personal accounts or devices must be furnished under public-records law; compliance with existing law (P77).
units.anchor: Users that have University records contained in their personal email accounts

units.why: 'periodically reviewed and revised' says the guidelines are provisional and will be updated with stakeholder feedback (P54).
units.anchor: will be periodically reviewed and revised by the appropriate governing bodies

documents.title: Developing a Syllabus Statement for AI
tiers: allowed for some assignments or purposes
documents.summary: Guidance for instructors on writing an AI syllabus statement, with three sample statements from permitted to not allowed. It recommends discussing the policy first day and lists prohibited actions in the ban sample.
documents.stance_why: The page gives instructors three sample statements: 'permitted or encouraged', 'allowed for some assignments or for some purposes', and 'not allowed'. Because it offers templates and leaves the choice to instructors, the stance is delegates with tiers.

units.why: It states it is 'good teaching practice' to be clear about what is allowed and recommends an AI statement in the syllabus; this asks instructors to state AI expectations (P09).
units.anchor: We recommend that you include an AI statement in the syllabus

units.why: The same sentence recommends instructors 'discuss it with your students on the first day of class', which goes beyond listing the rule (P66).
units.anchor: discuss it with your students on the first day of class

units.why: 'Include a detailed statement on AI use. Clearly define what assignments involve AI' asks instructors who allow AI to put detailed rules in the syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: Include a detailed statement on AI use.

units.why: 'You may consider co-creating course guidelines' with students: instructors set AI rules with students (P67).
units.anchor: co-creating course guidelines for the acceptable use of generative AI with your students

units.why: 'Redesigning assignments thoughtfully to integrate AI is crucial' says assignment design should change around AI (P35).
units.anchor: Redesigning assignments thoughtfully to integrate AI is crucial

units.why: For classes that ban AI, 'Clear AI policies and definition of inappropriate use should be provided', an instruction to state expectations in the syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: Clear AI policies and definition of inappropriate use should be provided.

units.why: 'You may need to rethink how you assess student learning' where AI is banned; assessment is to be reworked around AI (P35).
units.anchor: You may need to rethink how you assess student learning.

units.why: Sorts faculty views into 'permitted or encouraged, allowed for some assignments or for some purposes, and not allowed': named categories of use (P05).
units.anchor: fall loosely into 3 categories: permitted or encouraged, allowed for some assignments

units.why: Says acceptability is 'influenced by course and assignment learning goals', tying AI decisions to learning objectives (P83).
units.anchor: influenced by course and assignment learning goals

units.why: The permitted sample says 'you are welcome to use generative artificial intelligence/large language model tools', a permit/encourage default for the course (P02).
units.anchor: you are welcome to use generative artificial intelligence/large language model tools
units.frag_start: In this course you are welcome

units.why: The sample ties AI use to 'the course learning outcomes', saying AI use must align with course goals (P83).
units.anchor: Using these tools aligns with the course learning outcomes

units.why: The sample asks students not to 'enter your confidential information as part of a prompt' because AI companies store personal information (P50).
units.anchor: please do not enter your confidential information as part of a prompt
